name: Construct 3
tagline: Browser-based 2D game engine where logic is built from visual event sheets instead of code.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Construct 3 is not one app, it is an editor, a runtime, a renderer, a physics layer, an animation tool, a tilemap tool, a behavior library, and an export pipeline that targets web, desktop, and mobile stores. An agent can absolutely produce a canvas game loop with sprites and collision in a session, and that is genuinely fun. What it cannot produce is the thousand small affordances that make a visual event sheet usable by someone who does not write code, or the runtime hardening that keeps a game at 60fps on a five year old Android. The honest comparison is not Construct versus your weekend build, it is Construct versus writing the game directly in TypeScript, which is a reasonable choice if you are a programmer. If you are not a programmer, the editor is the entire product and you are not replacing it.
coreLoopDIY: A local Vite plus TypeScript canvas editor where you place sprites in a scene, attach a few canned behaviors, wire simple condition and action rows, hit play, and export a self-contained HTML file.
requirements: Your own sprite and audio assets
Comfort with TypeScript when the visual layer runs out of road
whatYouLose: Mature WebGL renderer with batching, effects, and tested mobile performance
Hundreds of behaviors and plugins that already handle pathfinding, platformer movement, tilemaps, and physics
One-click export to desktop, Android, iOS, and storefront-ready bundles
Built-in animation editor, tilemap editor, and asset pipeline
Documentation, tutorials, example projects, and a forum full of people who hit your bug in 2019
moatNotes: Game engines are the classic case where the surface is simple and the depth is fifteen years of edge cases: input handling, audio unlocking on iOS, frame pacing, save formats, export signing.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative to Construct is not a smaller Construct, it is writing the game yourself. Construct's customers are mostly people who want a finished playable thing and do not want to learn a language to get there, plus educators who need something that runs in a school Chromebook browser with no install. A personal clone of the editor serves neither group: you would have to be a programmer to build it, and if you are a programmer you would skip the editor and write the game. The license cost is trivial next to the weeks of engine plumbing it removes.
notes: A canvas game loop is a one-shot; an engine is not. The moat is a decade of runtime edge cases plus an editor usable by people who cannot code, which is the only audience that needs it.
prompt:
Build a local, offline 2D game editor and runtime called "TinyForge". Not a Construct clone, a deliberately small one.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + TypeScript, vanilla DOM for the editor UI, no framework.
- Canvas 2D for rendering. No WebGL, no game engine dependency.
- No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no network calls at all.

Editor (single page, three panes):
- Left: object type list. Create a type from an image file, set a name, frame count for a horizontal spritesheet, and collision box.
- Center: scene canvas with grid snap, click to place instances, drag to move, delete key to remove.
- Right: inspector for the selected instance (x, y, scale, angle) and behavior checkboxes.

Behaviors, implement exactly these five and no more:
- EightDirection (arrow keys, speed param)
- PlatformerBasic (left/right + jump, gravity param, ground collision against solids)
- Solid (marks instances as collidable)
- BulletMove (angle + speed, destroy when offscreen)
- DestroyOnCollision (pick a target type)

Event sheet:
- A table of rows. Each row has one condition and one action, chosen from dropdowns.
- Conditions: OnStart, EveryTick, KeyPressed(key), OnCollision(typeA, typeB), VariableEquals(name, value).
- Actions: Spawn(type, at instance), Destroy(instance), SetVariable(name, value), AddToVariable(name, n), PlaySound(file), GoToLayout(name).
- Global variables panel with name and initial numeric value.

Runtime:
- A Play button that runs the scene in an overlay with fixed 60Hz logic step and delta-time rendering.
- AABB collision only. Keep it readable over clever.

Project and export:
- Project state is one JSON object. Save and load from localStorage plus download/upload as .tinyforge.json.
- Export button produces a single self-contained index.html with assets inlined as base64 and the runtime inlined, playable by double clicking.

Out of scope, do not build: animation timeline editor, tilemap editor, pathfinding, physics engine, multiplayer, mobile export, plugin system, undo history beyond a single step.

Ship a README that states plainly what this is and is not, plus one example project (a platformer with a player, three solid blocks, and a coin that increments a score variable) loaded on first run.
No secrets needed; if you add any config later put it in .env and gitignore it.
